summary: In this fiction excerpt from a longer book, Anda and Lucy are playing an online game when Raymond, a player, shows them photos of impoverished children working at computers, a shantytown, and a family in a shack. Lucy wants to kill Raymond, who is trying to get them to understand the gold-farming workers behind the game economy. Anda defends Raymond, and the argument turns into a sword fight between the two women, which Anda wins.
one_line: In a fiction excerpt, two players argue over a gold-farming workforce in an online game, and Anda fights Lucy over whether to hear out Raymond.
key_facts: Raymond shows photos of fifty or more ranked little girls, in clean simple t-shirts, sitting at generic white-box PCs with hands on the keyboards.
The photos show a shantytown of corrugated aluminum and trash shacks with muddy trails, spraypainted graffiti, and rude boys loitering.
A third photo shows three little girls and a little boy on a battered sofa, with their mother serving something white and indistinct on plastic plates.
Lucy says she killed Raymond last time and promised to do it again if he tried to show her photos.
Raymond types that the workers are wrecking the game economy and providing a gold-for-cash supply that lets rich assholes buy their way in.
Raymond argues that if the workers do not play the game, they do not eat, so they care about the game as much as the players do.
Raymond tells Lucy that she is paid cash to kill these workers and so needs to play for her money too, making her and them 'a little the same.'
Anda's character clobbers Lucy barehanded, so that Lucy's avatar reels and drops its bow.
Anda tells Lucy, 'I don't want you to hurt him. I want to hear him out.'
Lucy's voicelink drops when her avatar attacks Anda, and Anda types one-handed while drawing her own sword.
Lucy has more experience points than Anda, but Anda is the better player and knows it.
Anda drives Lucy back down the road they had marched together until Lucy breaks and runs.
